content.thinking: The root मल्ल is bhvādi ātmanepada (मल्लते), so the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada madhyama bahuvacana form is मल्लिषीध्वम्/मल्लिषीढ्वम्, since it's seṭ with iṭ augment before ṣīdhvam, and after the i of iṇ, dh becomes optional.

The root शील (curadi, meaning उपधारणे) takes णिच्, and checking the pada assignment, the parasmaipada benedictive 2nd singular would be शील्याः, with णिच् lopa before the आर्धधातुक यसुट् per णेरनिटि. The आत्मनेपद form would be शीलयिषीष्.

I'm checking the root त्वर् — bhvādi, ātmanepadī with ghaṭādi/mit classification, giving त्वरते in present tense. For āśīrliṅ ātmanepada madhyama bahuvacana, the ending would be -sīdhvam, and I'm confirming त्वर् is ādit based on the ā in ञित्वरा.

Rule 7.2.16 bars iṭ for niṣṭhā, but त्वर् is seṭ since its vowel is udātta, so āśīrliṅ should take iṭ before ṣīdhvam. By rule 8.3.79, when iṭ follows a root ending in इण् (which includes र), the dh becomes optionally ḍh — giving त्वरिषीढ्वम् or त्वरिषीध्वम्, and I'll go with त्वरिषीध्वम्.

I'm trying to recall which gaṇa the root अर्थ (meaning "to request/beg") belongs to — checking whether it's curādi and ātmanepadī, and whether it falls under the kathādi/ākusmīya list of adanta roots.

Continuing the kathādi list, अन्वेषणे" through "गर्व माने" form the ātmanepadī subgroup, so अर्थ conjugates as अर्थयते, giving लुट् उत्तम एकवचन as अर्थयिताहे.

I'm working through the causative aorist of लाभ् (curādi, लाभयति) — applying णिच् plus चङ् luṅ formation, shortening the upadhā vowel of लाभि to get लभ्, then checking whether reduplication yields अललभत् given सन्वद्भाव rules when a laghu syllable follows in चङ्.

Weighing whether the सन्वत् (इ-substitution for abhyāsa) applies here: since लभ् after reduplication has ल followed by a short vowel and single consonant भ, it counts as laghu, triggering सन्वत् to give अलीलभत्, with the long reduplicated vowel from दीर्घो लघोः. I'm cross-checking against the causative of लभ् (लम्भयति, which takes नुम्) to confirm लाभ as a separate curādi root takes mandatory ह्रस्व rather than an optional rule, settling on अलीलभाम् as the first person form.

I'm checking the accent marking on this root द्राहृँ — the anudatta on the vowel suggests it's ātmanepadi, and being marked ऋदित् (ṛdit) matters for how it forms certain derivatives. This points to the dhatupatha entry "द्राहृ निद्राक्षये निक्षेपे च" in the ātmanepada section.

Now I'm working through the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada madhyama-bahuvacana form (-सीध्वम्), figuring out whether it takes seṭ (iṭ augment) and how 8.3.79 (विभाषेटः) applies — the rule that optionally changes स् to ष् when iṭ precedes षीध्वम्, giving options like द्राहिषीध्वम् or द्राहिषीढ्वम्.

Both forms are grammatically valid, so I'll go with द्राहिषीध्वम् as the answer.

I'm checking the root गवेष (मार्गणे, "to search"), which is an a-ending root forming गवेषयति in causative. For lun, I need to work out the reduplication and whether sanvadbhāva is blocked since this is an aglopī root, looking at the first syllable for reduplication purposes.

Following the pattern of कथ → अचकथत्, गवेष gives reduplication जगवेष, so the lun forms work out to अजगवेषत् (3rd sg) and अजगवेषः (2nd sg).

For ष्टुञ् (stu, to praise), ubhayapadi root, I'm working out the āśīrliṅ (benedictive) form. For parasmaipada third person singular I get स्तूयात्, and for second person plural it would be स्तूयास्त.

I'm checking the root प्लेव् meaning "to serve," noting it's listed among ātmanepadī roots with anudātta accent, so despite being in kartari (active voice) prayoga, it takes ātmanepada endings by virtue of being anudāttet.

For the liṭ madhyama bahuvacana ātmanepada form, the ending ध्वम् becomes ध्वे since the root is seṭ. Applying the reduplication rule where ए becomes इ (short) in the abhyāsa, प्ले reduces to पि, giving पिप्लेविध्वे — and optionally पिप्लेविढ्वे since iṭ is preceded by यण् (व), allowing the ढ substitution per विभाषेटः.

I'm recalling that पर्ण meaning "to become green" belongs to the adanta roots in the curadi gana, alongside others like कथ, वर, गण, and शठ in the Dhatupatha listing.

Continuing through the list of roots, I'm trying to recall more entries like स्मापने, शूर for valor, स्थूल, सूत्र for binding, मूत्र, पार/तीर for completing work, and working toward the पर्ण entry meaning "to become green."

I'm continuing to recall more entries from this dhātu list, moving through the ātmanepadī section and into the adanta roots before trailing off mid-list.

For luṅ with ṇic, the a of parṇa drops via अतो लोपः, and since this lopa counts as sthānivat, it blocks both upadhā-hrasva and sanvadbhāva — so I get parṇi, then need to work out the reduplication for caṅ since the stem starts with a consonant cluster.

Working through the reduplication: णि drops via णेरनिटि, then caṅ-reduplication gives पपर्ण following हलादिः शेषः (keeping only the first consonant with its vowel). Since sanvadbhāva doesn't apply here due to the ak-lopa condition, there's no इ-insertion, and I'm checking whether दीर्घो लघोः (which lengthens the abhyāsa vowel) only triggers when sanvadbhāva itself applies.

Since that long-vowel rule's anuvṛtti traces back to the same "अनग्लोपे" condition, aglopa blocks it here too, and पर्ण isn't even laghu since the r+ṇ conjunct makes the vowel guru anyway. So the form comes out to अपपर्णत्, matching the pattern seen in अववर्णत् from वर्ण, giving the dual अपपर्णताम्.

I'm trying to recall whether the root कृप (meaning दौर्बल्ये) belongs to the curādi class and whether it takes ātmanepada endings, checking through various Dhatupatha listings to pin down its classification.

Checking the ākusmīya ātmanepadī group in curādi, I confirm कृप isn't listed there. For कृप दौर्बल्ये, I recall that with ṇic the guṇa of ṛ produces कर्प, which the rule कृपो रो लः then converts r to l, yielding कल्प and ultimately the form कल्पयति.

Since it's parasmaipadī by default here, the lut uttama bahu form should be कल्पयितास्मः.

I'm checking the accent mark on this root to determine if it's ātmanepadī, comparing it against similar Dhatupatha entries like sevṛ, gevṛ, glevṛ meaning "to serve."

For the liṭ ātmanepada madhyama bahuvacana form, I'm working through the reduplication rule where the initial consonant kh becomes c, giving the abhyāsa "chi," then applying the iṭ augment with the optional ḍh/dh alternation per 8.3.79, arriving at चिखेविध्वे with चिखेविढ्वे as the optional variant.

I'm checking the Dhatupatha's curadi gana for the root शूर meaning "to be valiant," noting it belongs to the ātmanepadi subset known as the आकुस्मीय group.

So the present stem is शूरयते, and the first person singular optative (vidhiliṅ ātmanepada) would be शूरयेय.

I'm trying to locate the root पष in the Dhatupatha, checking whether it's an adanta root in the curadi list, since that would determine how the causative form is derived without vriddhi due to the अतो लोप rule.

I'm recalling the specific adanta list in curadi where पष appears with "अनुपसर्गात्" qualifier, alongside पत गतौ वा, स्वर आक्षेपे, रच प्रतियत्ने - confirming पष belongs to this group so it takes अ before the ति/सिप् endings.

I'm tracing the root पर्ण (parṇa, meaning हरितभाव/to turn green) in the curadi class, noting it's an adanta root ending in a, so with the causative णिच् the final a drops giving parṇi. Since it's adanta there's no upadhā guṇa issue in the aorist formation.

Checking the prohibitions for upadhā hrasva and sanvadbhāva that don't apply here since it's अग्लोपी, I work through the reduplication like कथ → अचकथत्, getting पर्ण → अपपर्णत् for third person, and अपपर्णत for second person plural.
I'm checking that भाज is listed among the adanta curādi roots, so applying णिच् gives भाजयति without needing vṛddhi since the vowel is already ā; for lot madhyama bahu parasmaipada it becomes भाजयत.

The anubandha अँ with anudatta accent marks this as atmanepadi, so गल्ह् takes atmanepada forms. For Lit madhyama purusha bahuvacana, it's जगल्हिध्वे/जगल्हिढ्वे, with the full atmanepada paradigm being जगल्हे, जगल्हाते, जगल्हिरे, जगल्हिषे, जगल्हाथ.

Rule 8.3.79 (विभाषेटः) applies here since the iṭ augment is preceded by ह्, which falls within the iṇ pratyahara (ह य व र ल from हयवरट्, लण्). This makes the ष्→ढ् substitution optional, giving both जगल्हिढ्वे and जगल्हिध्वे as valid forms — I'll settle on जगल्हिध्वे.

I'm identifying the root अर्थ as a curadi ātmanepada verb meaning "to request/beg," building its present tense form अर्थयते, then working out the लृङ् (conditional) conjugation across all persons and numbers in ātmanepada.

The augment आट् applies since the root form starts with a vowel, so अर्थयिष्यथाः becomes आर्थयिष्यथाः.

I'm trying to recall which gana the root सत्र (meaning सन्तानक्रियायाम्) belongs to, checking whether it's in curadi and if it's parasmaipadi or atmanepadi.

Continuing through the remaining ākusmīya roots list, I confirm सत्र doesn't belong there, so I'm checking the kathādi group of curādi roots instead, scanning through that enumeration to see where सत्र might fit.

I'm continuing through this list of root verb meanings - covering usage, concealment, separation, affection, diminishment, sound, distress, signaling, invitation, theft, movement, seizure, searching, astonishment, valor, and various other classical Sanskrit dhātu senses in sequence.

Since these roots are specified as ātmanepadi regardless of where the fruit of action goes, the answer stays सत्रयिष्यसे.

I'm trying to recall the curadi root for वठ, searching through similar roots like वटि and वट with meanings related to division or texts.

Actually, I think वठ ग्रन्थे belongs to the kathadi (अदन्त) group alongside वट and पट, which take forms like पटयति without vriddhi -- so वठ would likely form वठयति, with the dual उत्तम being वठयाव.

I'm trying to recall whether "kuṇa āmantraṇe" belongs to the ākusmīya group of curādi roots that take ātmanepada, searching my memory for the exact list of roots in that category.

I'm continuing through the dhātupāṭha list, noting more roots with their meanings — kaṇa for closing eyes, jabhi for destruction, ghaṭa for union, mokṣa for releasing, arha for worship, jña for enjoining, and several others, tracking which conjugation class they fall under.

I'm continuing through the dhātupāṭha list, noting entries like kūṭa for paritāpa and then landing on "saṅketa grāma kuṇa guṇa ca āmantraṇe" as roots meaning invitation or address.

For kuṇa, since it's a kathādi (adanta) root, the final 'a' drops before 'ṇic', so there's no upadhā guṇa — giving kuṇayati. In vidhiliṅ that becomes kuṇayet in parasmaipada, so the answer is कुणयेत्.

I'm trying to recall the exact root and meaning of कुण in the curadi gana of the Dhatupatha, checking whether it's listed as आमन्त्रणे (meaning "to invite/address") and whether it takes atmanepada endings.

I'm now recalling that कूण (meaning सङ्कोचने, to contract) appears in the list of roots taking atmanepada within that आकुस्मीय section, while कुण आमन्त्रणे likely belongs instead to the अदन्त कथादि group alongside roots like कथ, वर, गण, शठ.

Since it's adanta, अतो लोपः applies, so no guna of the उपधा by स्थानिवद्भाव — giving कुणयति. For लोट् उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन परस्मैपद, the form is कुणयानि (आत्मनेपद would be कुणयै, but here परस्मैपद fits).

The root रस falls under the curādi class (adanta), where आस्वादनस्नेहनयोः gives its meaning. With णिच् affix, अतो लोपः applies giving रसयति as the causative form, and रसितारौ for lṭ. I'm checking whether curādi adanta roots are generally ubhayapadi.

I'm checking the root सङ्केत, an a-ending (adanta) root meaning आमन्त्रणे, similar to कथ. Since it ends in a, that vowel drops before णिच् without guṇa or vṛddhi, giving सङ्केतयति, and the third person plural form सङ्केतयन्ति.
I'm working out the perfect tense forms for क्री in second person plural, checking parasmaipada and atmanepada endings separately to get चिक्रिय and चिक्रियिध्वे/चिक्रियिढ्वे right.

I'm trying to recall whether कृप in the curādi class (दौर्बल्ये, meaning weakness) takes ātmanepada endings, checking if it belongs to the ākusmīya gaṇa of self-voice verbs.

I'm going through the standard list of ākusmīya roots—चित, दशि, दसि, तर्ज, भर्त्स, शठ, यक्ष, गूर, लक्ष, त्रुट, वृष, मद, विद, मान, and others—to see if कृप appears among them. Since it doesn't, I conclude कृप must be parasmaipada instead.

Now I'm checking whether कृप follows the कृपो रो लः rule (8.2.18), which would turn it into क्लृप् form, but I'm uncertain whether this applies to the curādi-gaṇa reading of कृप specifically versus the "कल्पयति" form I recall from Siddhānta Kaumudī's "कृप दौर्बल्ये" entry.

Continuing through this list of Sanskrit dhatus with their meanings — covering roots for flowing, extending, cutting, splitting, obscuring, tearing, speaking clearly or unclearly, roaring, and desiring.

I'm trying to recall whether the curādi root kṛp (दौर्बल्ये) is distinct from the first-class kḷp, and whether this falls among the adanta roots like kath or var with their specific meanings.

Continuing through the curadi verb entries, I'm recalling more roots with their meanings - jasu for striking, pasha for binding, ama for disease, chata for breaking, ghata for assembling, and several others like arja, ghushir, lasa, and tasi relating to adornment and continuous action.

I'm trying to recall the continuation of the dhātu list — moving into the adanta roots like कथ (narration), and trying to place entries such as गुण, केत, कुण्ठ/गुण्ठ, पट/वट, रह, स्तन, and पत within their traditional meanings, though some of these I'm less certain about.

Now I'm remembering more clearly: the list continues with पष (without upasarga), स्वर (objection), रच (effort), कल (motion/counting), चह (deliberation), मह (worship), सार/कृप/श्रथ (weakness), स्पृह (desire), भाम (anger), सूच (slander), खेट (eating), क्षोट (throwing), गोम (smearing), कुमार (playing), शील (holding), साम (conciliation), and वेल (time-indication) — confirming that कृप belongs to the adanta class, so its forms like कृपयति skip guṇa since the final अ is elided.

For the causative aorist, with a-lopa happening before caṅ, I need to check whether 7.4.2's "nāglopiśāsvṭditām" blocks the upadhā-hrasva since the root underwent ak-lopa—that prohibition should keep the long vowel intact rather than shortening it.

Working through the sanvadbhāva prohibition for aglopi roots, there's no shortening applied, so reduplication proceeds normally: the abhyāsa takes "a" via urat (7.4.66), then haladiśeṣa and kuhoścuḥ operations give the final form अचकृपत् for third person, and अचकृपः for second person singular, paralleling how कथ् becomes अचकथत्.

I'm checking the root कासृँ, noting its anudātta accent marks it as ātmanepadī per the grammatical convention, and confirming it's explicitly cited in sūtra 3.1.35 despite not being ijādi since it starts with the consonant k.

Since this is periphrastic perfect (liṭ) for a root requiring the āma-pratyaya, I need to form कासाञ्चक्रे with the auxiliary कृ taking ātmanepada endings matching the main root per 1.3.63. For second person plural, the ṛ-ending before ढ्वे triggers the iṇ-rule converting dhve to ḍhve, giving कासाञ्चकृढ्वे as the final form.

I'm working out that बहि with the nasalized अनुदात्त इ marking signals it belongs to the आत्मनेपद class, recalling the Dhatupatha entry "बहि महि वृद्धौ" where both roots mean "to grow/increase."

For आशीर्लिङ् आत्मनेपद मध्यम बहुवचन, I apply the ध्वम् suffix and work through the सेट् augment, arriving at बंहिषीध्वम् — noting rule 8.3.79 allows an optional ढ substitution giving बंहिषीढ्वम् as well, since the ह falls within the इण् प्रत्याहार. I settle on बंहिषीध्वम् as the answer.
I'm checking the root वर्ण in Curadi, which is adanta and ubhayapadi, forming वर्णयति. For laṅ kartari prathama puruṣa bahuvacana parasmaipada, the form would be अवर्णयन्.

I'm checking the root क्नूय्'s accent markings to determine whether it's ātmanepadī, and whether it takes iṭ augment in the niṣṭha formation—trying to recall which anudātta-accented roots fall into this category.

For the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada madhyama puruṣa bahuvacana form, with iṭ inserted I get क्नूयिषीध्वम्. Since the sound preceding iṭ is य् (part of the iṇ pratyāhāra), rule 8.3.79 allows the optional ḍha substitution, giving both क्नूयिषीढ्वम् and क्नूयिषीध्वम् as valid forms, with the latter being the one I'll present.

I'm examining the root "ṇaya" (गतौ, meaning "to go/lead"), noting that the ṇ undergoes ṇ→n per ṇopadeśa rules, and that the anudātta accent marking indicates this root takes ātmanepada endings, giving forms like "nayate."

For the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada 2nd person plural, since nay is a seṭ root, the base form before sīdhvam requires iṭ augment. I work through the sandhi rules governing y+iṭ combinations (8.3.78-79), landing on nayiṣīdhvam as the optional ḍh-less variant alongside nayiṣīḍhvam.

I'm working out the liṭ ātmanepada form of त्रै (trai→trā), reduplicating to tatrā and applying the kit endings for second person plural, which gives -dhve.

Since trai is anit (not getting iṭ by default under the kṛtvarti exception rule), but liṭ actually requires iṭ for most roots except a specific listed group, I need to check whether trā falls into that excluded set — it doesn't, so iṭ applies, giving tatr+i+dhve via āto lopa, forming tatridhve. Then I'm checking whether 8.3.79's optional ḍh-substitution for dhve applies here, since the iṭ vowel is preceded by r, which falls under the iṇ pratyāhāra, making this an optional sandhi case.

I'm trying to recall the exact dhatupatha classification for निवास — whether it belongs to curadi with the meaning आच्छादने (to cover), treating it as an a-ending root rather than deriving it compositionally.

Adding णिच् gives निवासि, with no vrddhi since the vowel is already long, so the Lrt form comes out as निवासयिष्यति.

I'm examining the root शेवृ with its anudātta accent marking — this it-marker on the anunasika ṛ signals an ātmanepada verb meaning "to serve," grouped with similar roots like षेवृ, गेवृ, केवृ that all carry the same सेवने sense.

Working through the liṭ madhyama bahu ātmanepada form, I check rule 8.3.79 विभाषेटः, which makes the dh/ḍh substitution optional when iṭ follows a v (which falls within the iṇ pratyāhāra). After reduplicating śev to śiśev with the hrasva vowel change, adding iṭ and dhve gives शिशेविध्वे as the answer, with शिशेविढ्वे as the alternate form.
Working through the root नी for second person plural parasmaipada liṭ, I land on निन्य using the madhyama ending अ from थल् rules.

I'm checking that भाज belongs to the अदन्त roots listed in curadi gana (पृथक्कर्मणि), meaning when णिच् is added, the final अ is dropped and no उपधावृद्धि applies.

For Lun with चङ्, since भाज is अग्लोपी, the rule 7.4.2 नाग्लोपिशास्वृदिताम् blocks upadha hrasva, and since it's not an अनग्लोप case, सन्वद्भाव also doesn't apply. The reduplication follows the pattern like कथ → अचकथत्, giving अबभाजत् for singular and अबभाजताम् for dual.

I'm working through the perfect tense for पूङ् (bhvadi, ātmanepada), checking whether it's seṭ or aniṭ to determine if the ending takes इट् augment, giving forms like पुपुविध्वे or पुपुविढ्वे for second person plural, and considering the applicable sutra on vibhāṣā for iṭ after roots ending in इण्.

I'm checking whether रस belongs to the अदन्त (कथादि) group within curadi, trying to recall the list of roots that take that ending to see if रस fits among them.

Yes, "रस आस्वादनस्नेहनयोः" is indeed part of this अदन्त group, so the form becomes रसयावः, with no vṛddhi since the अत् lopa is treated as sthānivat.

I'm tracing the root ष्मिङ् to स्मि, which is Atmanepada and anudātta, making it aniṭ. Now I'm working out the āśīrliṅ Atmanepada second person plural form, checking whether the rule governing roots ending in इक् applies here for the सिच् and इट् insertion.

Since स्मि ends in a vowel rather than हल्, the kit rule from 1.2.11 doesn't apply, so guṇa happens like in चेषीष्ट and नेषीष्ट, giving स्मेषीष्ट. For the second person plural, I apply the rule that changes ध् to ढ् after an aṅga ending in इण्-class sounds, since स्मे ends in e, which falls under इण्, yielding स्मेषीढ्वम्.
